questions.question: Pipe P can fill a tank alone in 7 hours. Pipe Q can fill the same tank alone in 13 hours. In how much time can they together fill the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two pipes **P** and **Q** filling a tank in **x** and **y** hours respectively, time taken together = (x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Time taken = (7 × 13) ÷ (7 + 13) = 91 ÷ 20 hours.

⇒ 91 ÷ 20 = 4.55 hours = 4 hours + (0.55 × 60) minutes.

⇒ 4 hours 33 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 33 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time for **Pipe P** = 7 hours, Time for **Pipe Q** = 13 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of individual times; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe P 7 91 units 13 
 Pipe Q 13 7 

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** of P + Q = 13 + 7 = 20 units/hour.

⇒ **Total Time** taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 91 ÷ 20 hours.

⇒ 91 ÷ 20 = 4 (11/20) hours.

⇒ Convert fraction to minutes: (11 ÷ 20) × 60 = 33 minutes.

⇒ Total Time = 4 hours 33 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr 33 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (fill tank), while outlet/leakage pipes have negative efficiency (empty tank).

Net Work Done

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, net work in 1 hour = (1/x) − (1/y).

Alternate Day/Hour Work

If pipes operate alternately, calculate the combined work for one full cycle (e.g., 2 hours) before finding total time.</p

• According to Hindu beliefs, this fair starts on the day of Makar Sankranti.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated to the Mughal empire?
questions.solution:

• He was the founder of the **Suri Empire**.

• He was a **Pathan from Bihar** who defeated the **Mughal emperor Humayun (1530-1540, 1555-1556)** and founded the **Suri Empire** in Northern India.​
 
• He ruled from **1540-1545**.
 
• The tomb was built in memory of Emperor Sher Shah Suri.
 
• The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is in the **Sasaram town**, state of **Bihar.**
 
• The **"Battle of Chausa"** was fought between the Mughal emperor, Humayun, and the Afghan emperor Sher Shah Suri.
 
• It was fought on 26 June 1539 at Chausa, located in the southwest of Buxar, now in Bihar.
 
• In this battle, Sher Shah defeated Humayun and crowned himself as **Farid al-Din Sher Shah**.
 
• The Mughal emperor **Humayan** again faced Sher Shah in the **Battle of Kanauj** and was **again defeated by him.**
